text:
jane.cust: Hi team — AcmeProd is seeing a sustained surge and says our Dedicated pool didn't scale quickly enough. They hit ~25% 429s and median latency jumped from 120ms -> 2.4s. Raising to P1 customer. ticket: https://redwood.support/t/ACME-4821 :exclamation:

sasha: thanks — can you paste the support ticket summary and customer account id? any recent config changes on their dedicated allocation?

jane.cust: account acme-prod-42. No config changes indicated from CS. They hit a scheduled marketing blast at 11:02 UTC. Attached customer's sample logs (snippet):
```
2026-03-15T11:02:12Z ERROR request failed status=429 model=gpt-medium reason="no healthy replica"
2026-03-15T11:02:14Z WARN enqueue delay ms=6200 route=/v1/generate
2026-03-15T11:07:00Z INFO fallback to hosted model=true
```

mike-oncall: copying my quick checklist — please run these from the support runbook and paste outputs: `redwoodctl autoscaler status --account acme-prod-42`, `kubectl -n redwood get pods -o wide --selector=account=acme-prod-42`, and `redwoodctl warmpool list --account acme-prod-42`. If you can't run, I can fetch.

sasha: I've grabbed outputs — pasted below. (sanitized)
```
$ redwoodctl autoscaler status --account acme-prod-42
autoscalerId: as-7f9
minReplicas: 2
maxReplicas: 30
desiredReplicas: 20
currentReplicas: 2
scalingState: scaling_up
lastScaleEvent: 2026-03-15T11:03:18Z
scaleCooldownRemaining: 210s
queueDepth: 480
probeFailures: 3
```

$ kubectl -n redwood get pods --selector=account=acme-prod-42 -o wide
NAME                                READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE    NODE
acme-serve-1                         0/1     Pending   0          6m    <none>
acme-serve-2                         1/1     Running   0          9m    node-gpu-12
acme-serve-3                         0/1     ImagePullBackOff  0  5m    node-gpu-14
acme-serve-4                         0/1     Pending   0          4m    <none>
```

$ redwoodctl warmpool list --account acme-prod-42
warmPoolSize: 1
warmPoolReady: 1
prewarmedModel: gpt-medium-1.2-q4
```

mike-oncall: OK — two immediate red flags: desiredReplicas jumped (20) but current stayed at 2. Also warm pool is only 1. Looks like scale actions are blocked (pods Pending / ImagePullBackOff). Need `kubectl describe pod` and `kubectl describe node` for the Pending pods and the ImagePullBackOff to see events.

eva-eng: I'll look at autoscaler logs. quick check: scalingState says scaling_up but `scaleCooldownRemaining` non-zero — it may be pacing because of repeated probe failures. Probe failures at 3 could have triggered exponential backoff on probe-driven scale. Also ImagePullBackOff implies registry or auth issue for that node.

sasha: `kubectl describe pod acme-serve-1 -n redwood` event snippet:
```
Events:
  Type     Reason       Age    From               Message
  ----     ------       ----   ----               -------
  Normal   Scheduled    6m     default-scheduler  Successfully assigned redwood/acme-serve-1 to <none>
  Warning  FailedScheduling  6m  default-scheduler  0/10 nodes are available: 10 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.
```

chris-sre: that explains Pending — cluster has no spare GPU nodes to place pods. Why didn't cluster autoscaler add nodes? Check cloud provider quota or node pool provisioning errors. Also ImagePullBackOff on other pods suggests node pools may be in bad state or image registry throttling. Run `gcloud compute operations list` or provider equivalent.

mike-oncall: I queried infra API: node pool scale requests were sent but cloud quota for GPUs is 0/40 available (account-level quota exhausted). There are also 3 pods stuck in ImagePullBackOff with events showing `Pull rate limited` from registry. So two root causes: account GPU quota exhausted and registry rate-limiting causing slow startup.

sasha: customer notes they have surge credit and reserved capacity but not for this particular region — their Dedicated cluster is hitting soft quota.

eva-eng: mitigation options (immediate):
- manually bump minReplicas to 6 to keep more warm instances (temp) — will only help if nodes can be provisioned or warm pool used
- increase warm pool size to 6 and populate with smaller model variant as prewarm (fastest)
- temporarily route ~20% of traffic to hosted fallback (we already see fallback true in logs)
- request emergency GPU quota increase from cloud provider (takes 10-30m)
- retry registry pull with backoff and escalate registry rate limits with engineering partner

mike-oncall: I'll open the provider quota request and flag for expedited review. chris — can you check node pool provisioning errors and whether spot/preemptible node types were rejected?

chris-sre: looking at provider events — node pool create failed with `QUOTA_EXCEEDED: GPUs requested (10) would exceed project quota (40) vs current usage 40`. So autoscaler cannot add more nodes. Also 2 node creation attempts timed out due to `ImagePullBackOff` on the init container (we use a small sidecar that pulls from private registry). Registry returned HTTP 429 for those pulls.

jane.cust: customer is asking what we are doing now. They're pretty upset that their campaign lost conversions.

sasha: interim customer message: "we're on it — routing some traffic to hosted, opening quota escalation and request for prewarm increase. We expect partial restoration in ~15-30m." :hourglass_flowing_sand: 

eva-eng: short repro steps for engineering triage (to reproduce in staging):
1) Create a dedicated deployment with minReplicas=2, warmPool=1, burst pattern 10x normal QPS.
2) Simulate registry rate-limit by returning 429 on image pulls or throttle network on init sidecar.
3) Exhaust GPU quota by launching dummy GPU nodes reservations in project.
Run traffic spike and observe `desiredReplicas` increasing while `currentReplicas` stays low and pods Pending/ImagePullBackOff.

sasha: logs from autoscaler during the event (trimmed):
```
[11:03:17] scale request desired=20 current=2 reason=queue_growth
[11:03:18] provisioning nodes requested=8 status=queued
[11:03:24] node provisioning failed reason=QUOTA_EXCEEDED
[11:04:00] scaling paused reason=probe_backoff backoff=60s
[11:05:10] node provisioning requested=6 status=queued
[11:05:30] registry pull failed status=429 count=4
[11:05:40] desired=20 current=2 -> fallback triggered
```

chris-sre: action items and owners:
- chris-sre: escalate cloud GPU quota and confirm ETA (in progress)
- mike-oncall: enable hosted fallback routing to reduce 429s by 30% (done)
- eva-eng: file registry rate-limit escalation with infra partner and add exponential retry for init pulls (assigned)
- sasha: send customer update and confirm future warm pool sizing (assigned)
- ops: consider increasing default warm pool min for customers with scheduled surges (follow-up)

mike-oncall: temporary customer remediation applied: routed 25% traffic to hosted, increased warmPool to 3 via `redwoodctl warmpool update --account acme-prod-42 --size 3` (populating in progress). manual `kubectl scale --replicas=6 deployment/acme-serve -n redwood` attempted but pods stayed Pending due to quota, so warmpool population helped.

jane.cust: customer replied: "thanks — appreciate the update. please keep us posted on ETA for full restore."

eva-eng: long-term follow-ups (to prevent recurrence):
- add autoscaler awareness for registry pull failures (treat sustained ImagePullBackOffs as a signal to fallback or prefetch images)
- surface account-level GPU headroom in the Console (alerts when quota < X%)
- support playbook: detect scheduled spikes and recommend warmPool bump + prefetch 24h before the campaign
- add metrics for probe backoff duration in the autoscaler dashboard

sasha: closing note: I've updated ticket ACME-4821 with all outputs and linked cloud provider request #Q-10023. will follow up when quota increase completes. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
